appraisal_events.evidence: les invités... étaient forcés de venir lui dire bonsoir... Certes il y avait de l'orgueil dans cette attitude... le sens luxueux, curieux... dans un tableau de Carpaccio ou de Véronèse... comme le Margrave
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator elevates Charlus as a commanding, almost operatic aristocratic figure whom every guest must greet, framed with real aesthetic admiration alongside acknowledged pride.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle me poussa vers lui d'un mouvement prétendu protecteur et volontairement inefficace qui me laissa en panne presque à mon point de départ. Telle est la lâcheté des gens du monde.
appraisal_events.explanation: Her outwardly gracious gesture to help introduce the narrator is exposed as a deliberately empty, cowardly performance, explicitly named by the narrator as society's characteristic cowardice.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme d'Arpajon fut plus lâche encore que Mme de Souvré... Ce pouvoir avait été encore affaibli par la liaison qu'elle avait eue avec le duc de Guermantes; l'abandon de celui-ci y porta le dernier coup
appraisal_events.explanation: She is explicitly named as even more cowardly than Mme de Souvré in refusing the narrator's introduction request, a cowardice rooted in her already diminished, waning social power after being abandoned by the duc de Guermantes.

appraisal_events.evidence: beaucoup de regards s'étant levés vers un balcon... se penchait... la magnifique duchesse de Surgis-le-Duc, celle qui venait de succéder à Mme d'Arpajon dans le cœur de Basin de Guermantes... son corps envolé de Victoire
appraisal_events.explanation: Many guests' eyes are drawn to her as a strikingly beautiful, statuesque figure, and she has just supplanted Mme d'Arpajon as the duc de Guermantes's favorite, marking a clear comparative rise over her.

status_effects.explanation: Every guest is shown forced to come pay him respects, publicly confirming his central, dominant position at the party.
The narrator personally admires him as an almost mythic aesthetic figure, beyond the pride noted in his bearing.
Directly named by the narrator as an instance of society's cowardice for feigning help while ensuring it fails.
Left almost back where he started, still excluded from access to the prince despite the ostensibly protective gesture.
Explicitly judged even more cowardly than Mme de Souvré for pretending not to hear the narrator's request.
Her social power is described as already weak and further broken by the end of her liaison with the duc de Guermantes.
She visibly commands the attention of many guests and is marked as the duc de Guermantes's new favorite.
She is shown visibly vexed as public attention turns to the woman who has just replaced her in the duc de Guermantes's affections.
